# cloudinary_sub_account (Data Source)

Fetches a Cloudinary product environment (sub-account) by its `id` or by its `cloud_name`. Exactly one of the two must be set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look up a sub-account by its ID...
data "cloudinary_sub_account" "by_id" {
  id = "555asdf0000zxcvb3456qwerty"
}

# ...or by its cloud name.
data "cloudinary_sub_account" "by_cloud_name" {
  cloud_name = "scayle-acme"
}

output "tenant_cloud_name" {
  value = data.cloudinary_sub_account.by_id.cloud_name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `cloud_name` (String) The Cloudinary cloud name of the product environment to look up. Conflicts with `id`.
- `id` (String) The ID of the product environment (sub-account) to look up. Conflicts with `cloud_name`.

### Read-Only

- `api_access_keys` (Attributes List) The API access keys of the sub-account. The `secret` is not returned by the read API and is therefore empty here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_access_keys))
- `created_at` (String) The RFC 3339 timestamp when the product environment was created.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the product environment is enabled.
- `name` (String) The display name of the product environment.

<a id="nestedatt--api_access_keys"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_access_keys`

Read-Only:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the access key is enabled.
- `key` (String) The API key.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) The API secret. Not returned by the read API.
